name: Underreporter proposed changes
what_it_means: The IRS compared your tax return to forms other people sent in, like a W-2 or 1099. The numbers do not match, so the IRS proposes you owe more tax. This is not a bill yet. You can agree, disagree, or agree in part.
deadline_rule: 30 days from the notice date
documents_usually_needed: The CP2000 notice
Your Form 1040 for that tax year
W-2, 1099, and brokerage statements named on the notice
Any corrected payer forms

name: Underreporter inquiry
what_it_means: The IRS saw a mismatch between your return and other reports, and is asking questions first. It has not yet proposed a new tax amount the way a CP2000 does. Answer with records so they can close the question or send a later notice.
deadline_rule: 30 days from the notice date
documents_usually_needed: The CP2501 notice
Your return for that tax year
The income or deduction records the notice asks about

name: Notice of Deficiency (90-day letter)
what_it_means: The IRS says you owe more tax and is giving you a set window to go to Tax Court if you disagree. If you miss that window, the amount can be assessed and billed. This is a serious legal deadline, not a reminder letter.
deadline_rule: 90 days from the notice date (150 days if the notice is addressed to you outside the United States)
documents_usually_needed: The CP3219A notice of deficiency
The examination report or earlier notice it refers to
Your return and supporting records for that tax year

name: Balance due
what_it_means: The IRS says your return was processed and you still owe tax, penalties, or interest. This is a bill. You can pay, set up a plan, or explain why the amount is wrong.
deadline_rule: 21 days from the notice date (10 days if the amount is $100,000 or more)
documents_usually_needed: The CP14 notice
Your return and transcripts if you have them
Proof of any payment already sent

name: First reminder of balance due
what_it_means: The IRS already billed you and you have not paid the full amount. This is the first reminder. Interest keeps adding. Pay, dispute the amount, or ask for a payment plan.
deadline_rule: Pay as soon as you can; the notice asks for payment immediately
documents_usually_needed: The CP501 notice
The earlier bill it refers to
Proof of payments already made

name: Second reminder of balance due
what_it_means: The IRS has reminded you more than once that a balance is still open. If you ignore it, the next letters can talk about levies. Do not wait for a levy notice to answer.
deadline_rule: Pay as soon as you can; the notice asks for payment immediately
documents_usually_needed: The CP503 notice
Prior balance-due notices
Proof of payments or a payment-plan request

name: Intent to levy / Notice of intent to seize property
what_it_means: The IRS is warning that it may take state tax refunds or other property if you do not pay or appeal. This is past a simple reminder. You still have a short window to pay, set a plan, or appeal.
deadline_rule: 30 days from the notice date
documents_usually_needed: The CP504 notice
Proof of the balance and any payments
Collection appeal or installment papers if you are asking for time

name: Final Notice of Intent to Levy (Letter 1058)
what_it_means: This is the final levy warning. It also tells you that you can ask for a Collection Due Process hearing. If you miss the hearing window, the IRS can levy pay, bank accounts, or other property. People also know this letter as Letter 1058.
deadline_rule: 30 days from the notice date to request a Collection Due Process hearing
documents_usually_needed: The LT11 / Letter 1058 notice
Form 12153 if you are requesting a hearing
Financial information if you are asking for a plan or currently-not-collectible status

name: Math error, you owe
what_it_means: The IRS changed your return because of a math or clerical error and says the change means you owe money. You can accept the change or ask them to undo it. If you do nothing, the extra amount stands.
deadline_rule: 60 days from the notice date to request that the math-error change be undone
documents_usually_needed: The CP11 notice
Your original return
Workpapers that show the figure you filed

name: Math error, refund changed
what_it_means: The IRS changed your return because of a math or clerical error. The change usually lowers the refund they will send, or changes it to a small bill. You can accept it or ask them to undo the change.
deadline_rule: 60 days from the notice date to request that the math-error change be undone
documents_usually_needed: The CP12 notice
Your original return
Workpapers for the refund figure you filed

name: Data processing adjustment, balance due
what_it_means: The IRS changed your account after processing and now says you owe a balance. This can follow a later adjustment, not only a math error on the day they typed the return. Check the change against your records before you pay.
deadline_rule: 21 days from the notice date
documents_usually_needed: The CP22A notice
Account transcript if you have one
Proof of the item they adjusted

name: Estimated tax discrepancy
what_it_means: The IRS thinks the estimated tax payments you claimed on your return do not match what they have on file. That can create a bill even when the rest of the return is fine. Compare your cancelled payments or bank records to the notice.
deadline_rule: 21 days from the notice date
documents_usually_needed: The CP23 notice
Cancelled checks, bank records, or e-pay confirmations for estimated payments
Prior-year credit-elect records if you applied an overpayment

name: Overpayment applied to other debts
what_it_means: You were due a refund, but the IRS used it to pay another federal or state debt, or certain other legally collectible debts. This letter is usually telling you what happened, not asking you to file a new return. If the offset is wrong, you still need to write.
deadline_rule: No set protest clock on the face of a typical CP49; write as soon as you see an error
documents_usually_needed: The CP49 notice
Records of the debt they say they paid
Proof if that debt was already paid or is not yours

name: Audit of refundable credits (including EITC)
what_it_means: The IRS is holding or reviewing a refund because it wants proof of credits you claimed, often the earned income credit or similar credits. Send the documents they list. If you send nothing, they can deny the credit.
deadline_rule: 30 days from the notice date
documents_usually_needed: The CP75 notice
Proof of earned income (pay stubs, W-2, business records)
Proof of children or qualifying persons if a credit depends on them
Proof of residency and relationship as the notice lists

name: Identity verification
what_it_means: The IRS wants you to prove you are the person who filed the return, because something looked like identity theft or a suspicious filing. Until you verify, they will not finish processing. Use the method the letter names. Do not send your full Social Security number in a random email.
deadline_rule: 30 days from the letter date
documents_usually_needed: Letter 5071C
Photo identification the letter accepts
The return they are holding, if you have a copy

name: Notice of Proposed Assessment
what_it_means: California's Franchise Tax Board proposes that you owe more state tax. It is the state analog of a federal underreporter or proposed-assessment notice. You can agree, protest by the deadline, or pay.
deadline_rule: 60 days from the date of the Notice of Proposed Assessment to file a protest
documents_usually_needed: The FTB 4600 Notice of Proposed Assessment
Your California return for that tax year
Federal return and the records that support the protested items

agency: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
name: Statement of Proposed Audit Changes
what_it_means: New York State tax says an audit would change your return and proposes a new amount. You can agree, disagree, or agree in part. If you do nothing, the state can bill the proposed amount.
deadline_rule: 30 days from the notice date (follow the date printed on DTF-948)
documents_usually_needed: Form DTF-948
Your New York return for that tax year
The audit workpapers or schedules the form lists

name: Substitute for Return proposed amount
what_it_means: The IRS thinks you were required to file and did not, so it built a substitute return from the reports it has. That proposed return usually ignores deductions you could have claimed. File your own return or explain why you did not have to file.
deadline_rule: 30 days from the notice date
documents_usually_needed: The CP2566 notice
The return you are now filing, if you were required to file
Records of income and deductions for that year

name: Missing or incorrect taxpayer identification numbers
what_it_means: If you file 1099 forms, the IRS says some names or taxpayer numbers do not match their records. You may have to send backup-withholding notices to those payees and, later, withhold tax. This is a payer notice, not a bill for your own income tax.
deadline_rule: 15 business days from the notice date to send the required B-notice to payees, when the notice requires it
documents_usually_needed: The CP2100 notice and the list of mismatched accounts
Your Forms 1099 as filed
W-9 forms from those payees

name: Examination report
what_it_means: An IRS examiner finished a review and is sending the proposed changes in a report. You can agree and sign, disagree, or ask for a conference. If you disagree and do not answer, a later notice of deficiency can follow.
deadline_rule: 30 days from the letter date
documents_usually_needed: Letter 525 and the examination report
Your return for the examined year
Records for each proposed adjustment
